routes.description: Establish that neither deterministic causation nor indeterministic chance supplies the conscious authorship and alternative possibilities ordinarily attributed to free will.
routes.successCriteria: Show that reasons-responsive capacities and useful accountability practices can remain real while failing to establish ultimate authorship or desert-based moral responsibility.

motionBridge.description: Connect the absence of authorship under both determinism and indeterminism to the rejection of libertarian free will and ultimate moral responsibility.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the disputed concept centrally includes first-person authorship and a genuine ability to do otherwise.
Show that unchosen neural conditions and prior causes determine conduct without being authored by the conscious agent.
Separate pragmatically useful accountability from ultimate blame grounded in self-authorship.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use advance neural prediction to clarify why conscious awareness may follow rather than originate an action.
Concede differences in competence while denying that those differences create ultimate causal authorship.

routes.description: Establish that freedom worth preserving consists in reasons-responsive, self-controlling agency and does not require exemption from determinism or ultimate self-creation.
routes.successCriteria: Show that practical control, alternative capacities, and responsibility distinctions survive causal determination and support justified interpersonal and legal expectations.

motionBridge.description: Connect reasons-responsive agency under determinism to the forms of freedom and responsibility required by moral and social practice.

centralBridges.description: Define control through an agent's competence to respond to reasons across practical possibilities.
Ground the ability to do otherwise in real capacities and nearby counterfactual variation rather than identical-world replay.
Preserve responsibility by distinguishing normally capable agents from disabling impairment despite universal causation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain authorship through temporally extended planning and trained control rather than conscious selection of microscopic events.
Connect credible accountability practices to deterrence, cooperation, and stable mutual expectations.

sections.title: Conceptual stakes of free will
sections.rationale: The motion turns first on whether naturalistic agency preserves the relevant concept or omits authorship and alternative possibilities that define the dispute.

sections.title: Reasons-responsive agency and authorship
sections.rationale: This issue supplies the competing motion-level accounts of agency: conscious origination and genuine alternatives versus reasons-responsive practical control.

sections.title: Alternative possibilities and causal sensitivity
sections.rationale: The rival standards for doing otherwise determine whether deterministic counterfactual capacities answer or merely restate the challenge from causal dependence.

sections.title: Causal explanation and moral responsibility
sections.rationale: The responsibility burden depends on whether complete causal explanation erases culpability or leaves intact distinctions based on an agent's functional capacities.

sections.title: Neural prediction and macro-level control
sections.rationale: The prediction dispute tests whether preconscious neural production defeats authorship or remains compatible with temporally extended planning and trained control.
